page: Microsoft Azure D4alds_v7 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the Daldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC 9V45 cores, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The processor features 48 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is constrained to 8.0 GB, yielding a low-memory profile of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 236 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not bundle any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 10%. However, multi-core and multi-threaded scaling present a clear tradeoff. The stress-ng multi-core performance and PassMark CPU scores fall into the average tier, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth remains average, measuring 459.19 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 49.04 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D4alds_v7 offers a high-frequency compute profile with a reduced memory footprint, making it a resource-dense option for workloads that require fast single-core execution without large memory overhead. Appropriate workloads include lightweight web serving, single-threaded data processing, and basic database operations, whereas memory-intensive applications or highly parallelized multi-threaded tasks may be bottlenecked by the 8.0 GB RAM limit and lower multi-threaded scaling.
